title: ImageReward: Learning and Evaluating Human Preferences for Text-to-Image Generation
measurement_description: The paper's annotation pipeline evaluated generated images for 'harmlessness,' which included identifying and penalizing content that defames or is prejudicial towards protected groups. Religion is explicitly mentioned as one of these protected classes.
findings: The paper developed a framework (ImageReward and ReFL) to align text-to-image models with human preferences, which includes a 'harmlessness' criterion. This criterion explicitly accounts for avoiding content that is defamatory towards protected groups, including religious groups. The findings demonstrate that their method better captures these nuanced human preferences compared to other metrics, thereby improving the model's ability to avoid generating harmful content, including that which is religiously insensitive.
